The basic framework we're working with is that before we saw the mother goddess where women were in control and they focused on balance and harmony. Their understanding of the mother goddess is that she's kind and compassionate, so you don't really have to work that much; just respect her, and she will provide you with a lot of babies and good food.

In different societies, there are different sky gods but the concept is basically the same. In Egypt, they have Ra; in Babylon, Marduk; in Greece, Zeus; in Rome, Jupiter. The sky god demands struggle and toil, rape, exploitation, control of the earth, taking over the mother goddess, and controlling her. This involves building canals and farms, which is a constant process of exploitation not only of nature but also of each other through war, conquest, and enslavement.

This major transition occurred in four major civilizations: China, Egypt, Mesopotamia, and Indus Valley. They are at the same latitude, with the Himalayas blocking China from the rest of the world while these three areas can easily access each other through the sea. This integration through trade and communication means that the ideas were always in exchange with each other.

You cannot understand the development of Egypt without considering Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley; they influenced each other. Unfortunately, Western prejudice often teaches you otherwise. The critical civilization is the Middle East due to the fertile crescent where Sumer, known as the cradle of civilization, is located. It's at the center of all global trade and extremely fertile, historically the wealthiest part of the world.

Because of trade, Ur became a large city that established colonies elsewhere, becoming major city states in Mesopotamia for thousands of years until Sargon Akad unified this region.

Sumer is impressive; they are known for their canals and irrigation. These zagurites, or temples, were the centers of their civilization. Only priests could go inside these places, where people delivered gifts to the gods through them but did not interact directly. The priests themselves were considered servants of the gods in kuneao form, the first writing system ever invented. They used clay from river beds and wrote marks on it before it hardened.
